title: MATH GAOKAO - 261
description: Authentic-style mathematics problems inspired by China’s Gaokao — build deeper understanding, sharper thinking, and real exam readiness.

questions.learningObjective: Find the sum of two vectors in three-dimensional space.
questions.question: Given \(\vec{a}=(1,2,3)\) and \(\vec{b}=(4,-1,2)\), find \(\vec{a}+\vec{b}\).

questions.concept: Dot Product of Vectors in Space
questions.learningObjective: Calculate the dot product of two vectors in three-dimensional space.
questions.question: Given \(\vec{a}=(2,-1,3)\) and \(\vec{b}=(1,4,-2)\), find \(\vec{a}\cdot\vec{b}\).
questions.hint: Multiply corresponding components and add the results.

questions.concept: Cross Product of Vectors in Space
questions.learningObjective: Calculate the cross product of two vectors in three-dimensional space.
questions.question: Given \(\vec{a}=(1,0,2)\) and \(\vec{b}=(0,3,1)\), find \(\vec{a}\times\vec{b}\).
questions.explanation:
Using the determinant formula,
\[
\vec{a}\times\vec{b}
=
\begin{vmatrix}
\mathbf{i} & \mathbf{j} & \mathbf{k}\\
1 & 0 & 2\\
0 & 3 & 1
\end{vmatrix}.
\]
Compute each component:
\[
(0\cdot 1-2\cdot 3,\;2\cdot 0-1\cdot 1,\;1\cdot 3-0\cdot 0)=(-6,-1,3).
\]
questions.hint: Use the determinant form of the cross product.

questions.concept: Magnitude of a Vector in Space
questions.learningObjective: Calculate the magnitude of a vector given its components.
questions.question: Find the magnitude of \(\vec{v}=(3,-2,6)\).
questions.hint: Square each component, add, and then take the square root.

questions.learningObjective: Determine the cosine of the angle between two vectors using the dot product.
questions.question: Find the cosine of the angle between \(\vec{a}=(1,1,0)\) and \(\vec{b}=(1,0,1)\).
questions.hint: Use the dot product formula for the cosine of the angle between two vectors.

questions.learningObjective: Find the unit vector in the direction of a given vector.
questions.question: Find the unit vector in the direction of \(\vec{v}=(2,-2,1)\).
questions.explanation:
First find the magnitude:
\[
|\vec{v}|=\sqrt{2^2+(-2)^2+1^2}=\sqrt{4+4+1}=3.
\]
The unit vector is
\[
\frac{\vec{v}}{|\vec{v}|}
=\left(\frac{2}{3},-\frac{2}{3},\frac{1}{3}\right).
\]
questions.hint: Divide each component of the vector by its magnitude.

questions.learningObjective: Determine an unknown component so that two vectors are perpendicular.
questions.question: The vectors \(\vec{a}=(2,k,-1)\) and \(\vec{b}=(4,2,2)\) are perpendicular. Find \(k\).
questions.explanation:
Two vectors are perpendicular when their dot product is zero:
\[
\vec{a}\cdot\vec{b}=2(4)+k(2)+(-1)(2)=8+2k-2=6+2k.
\]
Set this equal to zero:
\[
6+2k=0 \implies 2k=-6 \implies k=-3.
\]
questions.hint: Set the dot product equal to zero and solve for \(k\).

questions.learningObjective: Calculate the scalar projection of one vector onto another.
questions.question: Find the scalar projection of \(\vec{a}=(2,1,2)\) onto \(\vec{b}=(1,2,2)\).
questions.explanation:
The scalar projection is
\[
\frac{\vec{a}\cdot\vec{b}}{|\vec{b}|}.
\]
Compute
\[
\vec{a}\cdot\vec{b}=2(1)+1(2)+2(2)=2+2+4=8,
\]
and
\[
|\vec{b}|=\sqrt{1^2+2^2+2^2}=\sqrt{1+4+4}=3.
\]
Thus the scalar projection is
\[
\frac{8}{3}.
\]
questions.hint: Use the dot product divided by the magnitude of the vector projected onto.

questions.concept: Area of a Parallelogram Spanned by Vectors
questions.learningObjective: Calculate the area of a parallelogram determined by two vectors in space.
questions.question: Find the area of the parallelogram spanned by \(\vec{u}=(1,2,1)\) and \(\vec{v}=(2,0,1)\).
questions.explanation:
The area is \(|\vec{u}\times\vec{v}|\). Compute the cross product:
\[
\vec{u}\times\vec{v}
=
\begin{vmatrix}
\mathbf{i} & \mathbf{j} & \mathbf{k}\\
1 & 2 & 1\\
2 & 0 & 1
\end{vmatrix}
=(2,1,-4).
\]
Then
\[
|(2,1,-4)|=\sqrt{2^2+1^2+(-4)^2}
=\sqrt{4+1+16}=\sqrt{21}.
\]
Therefore the area is \(\sqrt{21}\).
questions.hint: The area of the parallelogram equals the magnitude of the cross product of the two vectors.

questions.learningObjective: Calculate the volume of a parallelepiped using the scalar triple product.
questions.question: Find the volume of the parallelepiped determined by \(\vec{a}=(1,0,1)\), \(\vec{b}=(0,1,1)\), and \(\vec{c}=(1,1,0)\).
questions.explanation:
The volume is the absolute value of the scalar triple product:
\[
V=|\vec{a}\cdot(\vec{b}\times\vec{c})|.
\]
First compute
\[
\vec{b}\times\vec{c}
=
\begin{vmatrix}
\mathbf{i} & \mathbf{j} & \mathbf{k}\\
0 & 1 & 1\\
1 & 1 & 0
\end{vmatrix}
=(-1,1,-1).
\]
Then
\[
\vec{a}\cdot(\vec{b}\times\vec{c})
=1(-1)+0(1)+1(-1)=-2.
\]
Therefore
\[
V=|-2|=2.
\]
questions.hint: Use the absolute value of the scalar triple product of the three vectors.
